correctness.rationale: Forbidden row has probability 2^{-(k+1)}; every pair overlap is dominated by v_s^n and strict log-convexity v_s<q^{2-s/(k+1)} for shared s=1,...,k; equal-support distinct heads are incompatible. Valid dependency graph Stein-Chen gives critical Poisson; same bounds give supercritical second moment. Lower arities and empty supports vanish by monotonicity of rho_h. Standalone bounded checker verifies 12 exact expectations and 1585 overlap cases; infinity depends on analytic proof.

originality.rationale: No exact covering fixed-arity k>=2 supported proper Horn-implication Poisson-window theorem was found in actual searches and relevant texts. Stark (2004) explicitly covers unary subset comparison and presents a general Stein methodology and Boolean-relation illustration, so the use of Stein approximation and k=1 case are prior art. Bognar (1962) is a genuine residual risk: its general random-set results might dominate part of the new theorem but full text was not examined. The combination with positive-support minimal-premise and strict hierarchy is not stated in the inspected texts; no absolute priority is claimed.
residual_risks: Bognár 1962 original full text was not accessed, and its general treatment of random-set relations might imply Poisson counts or a stronger assertion.
Other general pattern-count theorems could imply the fixed-arity Poisson statement without the same terminology.
